title: Bolt a sprung storage-room door shut: hold it closed against its seal while sliding the bolt home
instruction: Bolt the door shut: hold it closed and slide the bolt into the keeper, then let go.
context: Bolting a door shut at lock-up is a core operation for janitors and building cleaners (about 2.4 million US workers in 2024, BLS employment projections, 37-2011). The difficulty is physical and bimanual: the door's seal pushes it 29 degrees open, so one arm must push it shut and keep pushing while the other slides a barrel bolt 3 cm along the door into the keeper; once the bolt is in, the keeper's lip holds the door and both arms let go. A bolt thrown with the door open fouls the latch post and the door can then no longer close.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the point midway between the two arm bases, which stand 61 cm apart: forward means away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. Door set (doorset, fixed): a small storage-room door in a light grey frame, its closed line 30 cm forward. The door (door joint, blue, 21 cm wide x 11 cm tall x 12 mm thick) hangs on a hinge post at 14 cm left (vertical axis) and is pushed 29 degrees open towards the arms by its seal (hinge spring 0.6 N m/rad); it closes against the frame. The latch post, 7 to 9 cm right, has a keeper slot 9.5 cm up with a lip on its near side. A brass barrel bolt (bolt joint) on the door's near face, 9.5 cm up, 5 cm long with a knob, slides 3 cm towards the latch post (friction 0.4 N). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The door is shut when its hinge is within 2 degrees of the frame stop; the bolt is thrown when it has slid at least 2.5 cm of its 3 cm travel. Score at the end of the trial: 0.3 for the door shut plus 0.3 for the bolt thrown (0 to 0.6). 1.0 when the door is shut and bolted, nothing moves (under 0.03 rad or 5 mm over the last 0.3 s) and no gripper tool point is within 5 cm of the door's face or the bolt knob, so that the bolt alone holds the door, held for 1 s (the trial then ends; completed less than 1 s before the run limit scores 0.6).
reset_notes: Draw the bolt back fully and let the door spring open; the frame stays fixed.
fidelity: Approximate. The door's seal is modelled as a hinge spring towards 29 degrees open; the barrel bolt is a friction-held slide; door, frame and keeper are rigid boxes. The keeper holds the door only by contact with the bolt. PhysX rigid-body contacts with default friction.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (door left sprung open and bolt not moved; hit the 120 s step limit); demo: 1.0 (one arm pushed the sprung door shut and held it against its seal while the other slid the barrel bolt into the keeper; both hands let go and the bolt held the door shut for 1 s)
